subject: how to deal with Exogenous nominal categorical variables

messages.author: b3726f30c8bb7288
messages.subject: how to deal with Exogenous nominal categorical variables
parts:
my dataset have nominal categorical variables, each have more than 2 items, I replace them by a set of $K-1$ dummy variables, but how to establish the models? the data like

v1(a,b,c) transformed to  x1,x2 two dummy variables
v2(d,e,f)  transformed to  x3,x4 two dummy variables
v3(g,h,i)  transformed to  x5,x6 two dummy variables

the initial structure of SEM model is like the below picture:
Model<-'Y ~ V1+V2+V3
              V3 ~ V1+V2'
partialMedSEM<-sem(Model, data=data)

when replace the variable, I establish a model like:
Model<-' r1~= x1+x2
               r2~= x3+x4
               r3~= x5+x6
             Y ~ r1+r2+r3
              V3 ~ r1+r2'
however, it doesn't work, how to deal with this problems ,thank you!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: how to deal with Exogenous nominal categorical variables
parts:
On 01/26/2015 03:20 PM, He Li wrote:
> my dataset have nominal categorical variables, each have more than 2
> items, I replace them by a set of $K-1$ dummy variables

> v1(a,b,c) transformed to x1,x2 two dummy variables
> v2(d,e,f) transformed to x3,x4 two dummy variables
> v3(g,h,i) transformed to x5,x6 two dummy variables
> the initial structure of SEM model is like the below picture:

> Model<-' r1~= x1+x2
> r2~= x3+x4
> r3~= x5+x6
> Y ~ r1+r2+r3
> V3 ~ r1+r2'

That does not make sense. Why do you use the "=~" operator here? You
should just replace the 'V's in your origin model by the dummy
variables, as in

Y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6

However, you can NOT have a nominal variable (with more than 2
categories) as a dependent variable (for now). So if 'V3' is a nominal
variable, lavaan (0.5-17) can not handle this. All you can do is reduce
it to a binary variable, or use different software.

Yves.
